p01.why: Two separate local variables are not one array, so their difference is undefined, and the Evidence says every compiler rejects it during constant evaluation.

p02.why: An unscoped enumerator, bool, and char all count as integers for pointer arithmetic; there is no main, and arr + 'a' - 'a' groups as (arr + 97) - 97, which would be undefined at run time (ADD-10) but the program is not run.

p03.why: A class operand without an operator+ or operator- is not one of the allowed operand forms.

p04.why: Pointers into one array subtract to the element count, negative when the first pointer comes earlier.

p05.why: Each operand pair gets the common type of the usual arithmetic conversions, -1 + 0u wraps to the largest unsigned value, and pointer plus integer keeps the pointer type.

p06.why: Two null pointers have difference zero, and adding or subtracting zero from a null pointer gives a null pointer.

p07.why: An enumeration plus a floating-point value is deprecated, Clang and GCC warn, and -Werror turns the warning into an error.

p08.why: Subtracting base pointers into two different derived elements is undefined; Clang and EDG reject it during constant evaluation, and GCC accepts it.

p09.why: Adding zero to a null pointer gives a null pointer, and the difference of two null pointers is zero.

p10.why: Additive operators bind tighter than shifts and looser than *, so every assertion holds.

p11.why: The pointer moves within the array, the reads are in bounds, and the difference is 2.

p12.why: int_max + 1 does not fit in int, and constant evaluation rejects the signed overflow.

p13.why: A base pointer into a derived array sees one object, so moving it by two is undefined; Clang and EDG reject, GCC accepts.

p14.why: The type of nullptr is not a valid operand of +.

p15.why: Unscoped enumerations, bool, and char are valid arithmetic operands and the values all match.

p16.why: Pointers to void are not valid operands; GCC gives a pedantic diagnostic, which -pedantic-errors makes an error, and Clang and EDG reject in all modes.

p17.why: a - 1 is before the first element; Clang and EDG reject it during constant evaluation, and GCC 14 and 16 accept the pointer.

p18.why: A single object counts as an array of one, so &x + 1 is a valid one-past pointer and the difference is 1.

p19.why: a + b is a prvalue, and & does not accept a prvalue.

p20.why: Moves inside the array in both directions and integer plus pointer are valid, and the reads give 3, 1, and 2.

p21.why: A scoped enumeration is not a valid operand of +.

p22.why: The sum is finite but past the largest double; Clang gives infinity, and GCC and EDG reject the constant.

p23.why: A base pointer moved one past its subobject is valid, and every compiler accepts a difference of 1 during constant evaluation.

p24.why: An unsigned char pointer steps through the 8 bytes of the long up to one past the end; the bytes are 1 to 8, sum 36, and the sanitizers report nothing.

p26.why: Pointer subtraction needs two pointers to the same type, and int* and long* differ.

p27.why: A pointer to a function is not valid in pointer arithmetic; -pedantic-errors makes GCC reject it too.

p28.why: With -m32 pointers are 4 bytes and p - q has type int.

p29.why: INT_MIN - 1 does not fit in int, and constant evaluation rejects the overflow.

p30.why: INT_MAX + 1 overflows at run time, and the undefined sanitizer stops the program with a nonzero status.

p31.why: argc is at least 1, so the taken path overflows and the undefined sanitizer stops the program.

p32.why: Arithmetic on void* is not valid; -pedantic-errors makes GCC reject it.

p33.why: Unsigned results wrap, and unsigned char promotes to int so 0 - 1 is -1.

p34.why: On x86-64 pointers are 8 bytes and p - q has type long.

p35.why: argc is 1, so the program moves a null pointer by a nonzero amount; the specification does not say whether the sanitizer stops this, so I predict undefined (Clang likely stops it, outside knowledge).

p36.why: Unsigned subtraction and addition wrap around.

p37.why: Differences count elements of Point, so they are 5, -5, 10, and 0.

p38.why: A nonzero offset from a null pointer is undefined, and all compilers reject it during constant evaluation.

p39.why: a + 3 is the valid one-past position, and end - a is 3.

p40.why: A scoped enumeration does not count as an integer for pointer arithmetic.

p41.why: The promotions and common types match each assertion; low + 0.5 only draws a deprecation warning, which does not stop translation without -Werror.

p42.why: A pointer operand must point to a complete object type.

p43.why: The pointers point into two different arrays, and constant evaluation rejects the difference.

p44.why: -6e38 is finite but outside float's range; Clang gives infinity, and GCC and EDG reject.

p45.why: Reading through a base pointer one past its subobject is undefined; Clang and EDG reject, GCC accepts.

p46.why: With -m32 the difference 2147483648 does not fit in int; Clang and EDG reject the constant, and GCC rejects the array as larger than INT_MAX bytes.

p47.why: Reading through the one-past pointer is undefined, and constant evaluation rejects the read.

p48.why: The operand order is unspecified, the program accepts either order, and the sum is 9.

p49.why: The operand order is unspecified, the program accepts either order, and the sum is 9.

p50.why: a + 4 is past the one-past position; Clang and EDG reject, GCC 14 and 16 accept the pointer.

p51.why: The signed sum overflows in a constant initializer.

p52.why: + and - group left to right, bind looser than * and tighter than <<, so all assertions hold.

p53.why: Adding two different enumerations is deprecated, the compilers warn, and -Werror makes the warning an error.

p54.why: Each row of a two-dimensional array is its own array, so p + 3 leaves row 0 and the read through it is rejected during constant evaluation.

p55.why: For -, the pointer must come first; an integer minus a pointer is not a valid form.

p56.why: With -m32 the difference type is 4 bytes, and differences of INT_MAX and -INT_MAX fit in int, which no compiler rejects according to the Evidence.
